text: Once a pipeline is published, every run it ever makes, triggered or manual, shows up in exactly one place: the Monitor hub, in the left sidebar of Data Factory Studio. This is genuinely where you'll spend most of your time once pipelines are in production — building them is honestly the smaller half of the job.

The default view lists every triggered pipeline run in the selected time window. Search by run ID or name, filter by status or time range, and every row shows exactly when a pipeline ran, how long it took, and what triggered it. Note the Refresh button — this view genuinely doesn't auto-refresh.

A pipeline status of Failed only tells you that something broke. Click the pipeline name, and you get the activity runs view — every single activity inside that run, in execution order, each with its own type, duration, integration runtime, and status. This is where real debugging actually starts.

Click the error icon on a failed activity, and Data Factory shows you the actual error: an error code, a failure type, and the raw exception text. Read the failure type first — here, User configuration issue points straight at a missing S3 bucket, not some transient network blip you'd otherwise have to guess at.

Switch from List to Gantt, and you get run history laid out over time, one row per pipeline, bars sized by duration. The list view answers what happened on this one run. The Gantt view answers how has this pipeline been behaving over the last week — reach for it when you're hunting a pattern, not a single failure.

Two genuinely different reruns exist. Rerun, from the pipeline runs list, restarts the whole pipeline from its first activity. Rerun from failed activity, from the activity runs view, restarts only from the activity that actually failed, skipping everything that already succeeded — a real difference when expensive activities ran successfully before the failure.

That's the Monitor hub: the runs list, activity-level drill-down, real error messages, and the Gantt view for spotting patterns. Next: Alerts, Metrics, and Retry Policies — getting notified the moment something breaks, instead of finding out only when you go looking.
